name: gitopsctl-phase1
notes: Names the phase 1 trust work: scoped API tokens, race fixes, and guarded pruning.

commits.subject: Phase 1 trust: API auth, safe prune and plan, race fixes, release hygiene, .verify harness (#55)
commits.body:
* refactor: share controller POST helper across check-cluster, sync-app, approve-app

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore: bump Go to 1.27.2 and update dependencies

Pins kube-openapi to the version required by apimachinery 0.37.1 and keeps
kustomize at 0.21.2 until they align.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore: bump golangci-lint pre-commit hook to v2.14.0 for Go 1.27

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(controller): remove channel-close race, stale runtime cleanup, unlocked cluster status writes

Stop no longer closes command channels (senders select on ctx.Done), is
idempotent, and runtime cleanup now compares the runtime identity instead of
addresses of local variables. saveAppStatus propagates LatestGitHash and
AppliedResources. Cluster health results are written under the clusters lock.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(api): release applications lock before triggering sync

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: run tests with the race detector

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(api): bearer-token auth with read/sync/admin scopes, audit events, opt-in CORS

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(cli,tui): send --api-token / GITOPSCTL_API_TOKEN to the API

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(start): load API tokens and bind loopback-only when none are configured

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: document API authentication flags

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(k8s): label applied resources with ownership, add guarded Prune

Applied objects now carry app.kubernetes.io/managed-by and gitopsctl.io/app|cluster labels.
Only NotFound triggers create; other Get errors are reported. Prune deletes stale
resources owned by the app, skips protected kinds, and refuses above a deletion limit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(app): add opt-in prune setting (register-apps --prune)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(controller): prune stale owned resources after a successful sync

Prune is opt-in per app, runs only after a clean apply, keeps unsettled
resources tracked, and rolls back LastSyncedGitHash on failure so the next
poll retries.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(k8s): read-only Plan of create/update/unchanged/prune

ApplyManifests now shares a renderManifests step with Plan. Plan compares rendered
objects against live state by subset match so API-server defaults do not show as drift.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(controller): PlanApp reports what a sync would change without applying

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(api): POST /applications/:name/plan returns a read-only sync plan

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(cli): diff-app shows what a sync would change

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: document --prune and diff-app

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(tui): close response body in bearer token test

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: write applications and clusters state atomically

A crash mid-write previously left truncated JSON that stopped the controller from starting.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(controller): idempotency and failure-recovery scenarios for sync

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore: add Apache-2.0 license

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: pin actions and tool versions by SHA, scope workflow permissions, pin base image digest

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* build: generate checksums and SBOMs and sign release artifacts with cosign

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(controller): keep reconciling after failed syncs, deliver manual approvals, stop health checks masking errors

- A failed first sync no longer ends the reconcile loop when a cluster client exists.
- Approvals recorded on the shared application now reach the reconciler's copy.
- checkHealth only runs for synced states so Error/OutOfSync are not overwritten by Healthy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(api): approving an unknown application returns 404

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: use the real snake_case config keys in docs and example configs

The examples used camelCase keys the loader never read, so examples/configs produced apps with no repo or cluster.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(verify): black-box integration scenarios against the real binary and a fake Kubernetes API

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(verify): scenario catalog, scored runner and kind e2e for agent-driven quality checks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: run the .verify scenarios; document them in CONTRIBUTING

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: bump govulncheck to v1.9.0, v1.1.4 panics on Go 1.27

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

+name: Continuous Testing
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches:
+      - master
+  pull_request:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  test:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout
+        uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803
+
+      - name: Setup Go
+        uses: actions/setup-go@924ae3a1cded613372ab5595356fb5720e22ba16
+        with:
+          go-version: "1.27.2"
+          cache: true
+
+      - name: Go build
+        run: |
+          go build -v ./...
+
+      - name: Run govulncheck
+        run: |
+          go install golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@v1.9.0
+          govulncheck ./...
+
+      - name: golangci-lint
+        uses: golangci/golangci-lint-action@ba0d7d2ec06a0ea1cb5fa41b2e4a3ab91d21278a
+        with:
+          version: v2.14.0
+
+      - name: Go fmt (check)
+        run: |
+          test -z "$(gofmt -l .)"
+
+      - name: Go test
+        run: |
+          go test -race -coverprofile=coverage.txt -covermode=atomic ./...
+          go tool cover -func=coverage.txt
+
+      - name: Check Coverage
+        run: |
+          # Parse coverage total from the func output
+          total_coverage=$(go tool cover -func=coverage.txt | grep total | awk '{print $3}' | sed 's/%//')
+          echo "Total coverage: $total_coverage%"
+          # Check if coverage is below 80% (using awk for float comparison)
+          if [ "$(echo "$total_coverage < 80.0" | bc)" -eq 1 ]; then
+            echo "Error: Coverage $total_coverage% is below the required 80.0% threshold."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+
+      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
+        uses: codecov/codecov-action@fb8b3582c8e4def4969c97caa2f19720cb33a72f
+        with:
+          files: ./coverage.txt
+          fail_ci_if_error: false
+
+      - name: Go vet
+        run: |
+          go vet ./...
+
+      - name: CLI smoke
+        run: |
+          chmod +x scripts/cli-smoke.sh
+          scripts/cli-smoke.sh
+
+  verify:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout
+        uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803
+
+      - name: Setup Go
+        uses: actions/setup-go@924ae3a1cded613372ab5595356fb5720e22ba16
+        with:
+          go-version: "1.27.2"
+          cache: true
+
+      - name: Run verification scenarios
+        run: .verify/run.sh --no-gates --no-e2e

+name: GoReleaser
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches:
+      - master
+    tags:
+      - "*"
+  pull_request:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  snapshot:
+    name: GoReleaser Snapshot Build
+    if: "!startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')"
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout
+        uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 0
+
+      - name: Setup Go
+        uses: actions/setup-go@924ae3a1cded613372ab5595356fb5720e22ba16
+        with:
+          go-version: "1.27.2"
+          cache: true
+
+      - name: GoReleaser (Snapshot)
+        uses: goreleaser/goreleaser-action@a4f02ab5355a589de60d917a659ce617ed19b3de
+        with:
+          distribution: goreleaser
+          version: v2.18.3
+          args: build --snapshot --clean
+
+  release:
+    name: GoReleaser Release
+    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    permissions:
+      contents: write
+      packages: write
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout
+        uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 0
+
+      - name: Setup Go
+        uses: actions/setup-go@924ae3a1cded613372ab5595356fb5720e22ba16
+        with:
+          go-version: "1.27.2"
+          cache: true
+
+      - name: Set up QEMU
+        uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@99012661954931238ded8c8b007157a8430204e1
+
+      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
+        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@f87e5991a6d7451dcb8d9637bfbc97413f497069
+
+      - name: Install cosign
+        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@6f9f17788090df1f26f669e9d70d6ae9567deba6
+
+      - name: Install syft
+        uses: anchore/sbom-action/download-syft@66cbf4bc1f1c0d2edc94016e65bc221b6bb0ad6c
+
+      - name: Login to GitHub Container Registry
+        uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f
+        with:
+          registry: ghcr.io
+          username: ${{ github.repository_owner }}
+          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+
+      - name: Generate GitHub App Token for Homebrew Tap
+        id: app-token
+        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510
+        with:
+          client-id: ${{ secrets.TAP_APP_ID }}
+          private-key: ${{ secrets.TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
+          owner: ${{ github.repository_owner }}
+          repositories: "homebrew-gitopsctl"
+
+      - name: Run GoReleaser
+        uses: goreleaser/goreleaser-action@a4f02ab5355a589de60d917a659ce617ed19b3de
+        with:
+          distribution: goreleaser
+          version: v2.18.3
+          args: release --clean
+        env:
+          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+          TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}

@@ -0,0 +1,54 @@
+# .verify
+
+Executable definition of "this gitopsctl is good". It is meant to be run by agents and humans after any change, and answers one question: **is it safe to ship?**
+
+```bash
+.verify/run.sh                         # everything: gates, scenarios, e2e (if available)
+.verify/run.sh --only S-SYNC-04,F-API-02   # just these scenarios while iterating
+.verify/run.sh --no-gates --no-e2e     # scenarios only
+.verify/run.sh --list                  # ids, kinds, severities, titles
+```
+
+The runner writes `.verify/report.json` and exits `0` only on verdict `PASS`.
+
+## What is checked
+
+| Layer | Where | What it proves |
+|-------|-------|----------------|
+| Gates | `scenarios.json` → `gates` | Build, vet, gofmt, golangci-lint, unit tests with `-race`, coverage ≥ 80%, tidy modules, govulncheck, GoReleaser config |
+| Integration scenarios | `integration/` | The real `gitopsctl` binary against real git repositories and an in-process fake Kubernetes API (`integration/fakekube_test.go`): auth, sync, manual approval, plan, prune, outages, recovery, CLI validation, docs and release hygiene |
+| Unit-backed scenarios | `scenarios.json` → `go-test` targets | Narrow behaviours that integration cannot reach cheaply: shutdown races, atomic state writes, prune guards |
+| End-to-end | `e2e/kind.sh` | Real API-server behaviour on kind. Skipped (not passed) when `kind`, `kubectl` or a Docker daemon is missing |
+
+Scenario ids: `S-*` are **success** scenarios (correct behaviour works), `F-*` are **failure** scenarios (bad input, outages and attacks are handled safely), `E-*` need a real cluster.
+
+## Reading the report
+
+```jsonc
+{
+  "summary": { "verdict": "PASS|CONDITIONAL|FAIL", "score": 98.01, "blocking_failures": ["S-PLAN-01"] },
+  "results": [{ "id": "S-SYNC-01", "kind": "success", "severity": "critical", "status": "pass|fail|skipped", "detail": "…" }]
+}
+```
+
+- **Score** = weight of passed ÷ weight of non-skipped, with critical=5, high=3, medium=2, low=1.
+- **PASS**: no failed critical/high scenario and score ≥ 95. **CONDITIONAL**: no failed critical and score ≥ 80. **FAIL**: otherwise.
+- `skipped` means the check could not run here, not that it passed. Report skips; do not count them as evidence.
+- `detail` holds the failing test names and their output. A test named in the catalog but absent shows as `missing`, which fails the scenario.
+
+## How an agent should use it
+
+1. Run `.verify/run.sh` before changing anything to get a baseline, and again before reporting completion.
+2. For each failure, read the scenario in `scenarios.json`: `given/when/then` is the contract and `if_failing` points at the likely cause.
+3. Fix the product code. Do not edit a scenario, weaken an assertion, or lower a threshold to turn a failure green. Change a scenario only when the intended behaviour changed, and say so in the report.
+4. A regression in any critical scenario blocks the change, whatever the score.
+
+## Adding a scenario
+
+1. Write the test. Integration tests live in `integration/` and are named `TestScenario_<ID with underscores>_<Description>` (`S-SYNC-01` → `TestScenario_S_SYNC_01_…`).
+2. Add an entry to `scenarios.json` with `id`, `kind`, `severity`, `given/when/then`, `verify.targets` (package plus exact top-level test names) and `if_failing`.
+3. Run `.verify/run.sh --only <ID>`; then break the product behaviour on purpose and confirm the scenario fails.
+
+The fake API in `integration/fakekube_test.go` implements only ConfigMaps, discovery and `/version`. Use `e2e/kind.sh` for anything that depends on real server behaviour (defaulting, field managers, other kinds).
+
+`go test ./...` ignores this directory because it starts with a dot; the runner invokes it explicitly with `go test ./.verify/integration`.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Real-cluster check for gitopsctl using kind. Prints "RESULT E-KIND-01 PASS|FAIL|SKIP <detail>".
+set -uo pipefail
+
+ID="E-KIND-01"
+ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
+WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
+CLUSTER="gitopsctl-verify-$$"
+PORT=$((20000 + RANDOM % 10000))
+KUBECONFIG_FILE="$WORK/kubeconfig"
+PID=""
+
+for tool in kind kubectl docker jq git curl go; do
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "RESULT $ID SKIP missing tool: $tool"; exit 0; }
+done
+docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "RESULT $ID SKIP docker daemon is not running"; exit 0; }
+
+cleanup() {
+  [[ -n "$PID" ]] && kill "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 && wait "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1
+  kind delete cluster --name "$CLUSTER" >/dev/null 2>&1
+  rm -rf "$WORK"
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT
+
+fail() { echo "RESULT $ID FAIL $1"; exit 0; }
+
+kc() { kubectl --kubeconfig "$KUBECONFIG_FILE" "$@"; }
+
+wait_for() { # description timeout command...
+  local description="$1" timeout="$2"; shift 2
+  local deadline=$((SECONDS + timeout))
+  while (( SECONDS < deadline )); do
+    "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
+    sleep 1
+  done
+  fail "timed out waiting for: $description"
+}
+
+app_synced() {
+  local status
+  status="$(curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/api/v1/applications/web" | jq -r .status)" || return 1
+  [[ "$status" == "Synced" || "$status" == "Healthy" ]]
+}
+
+(cd "$ROOT" && go build -o "$WORK/gitopsctl" .) || fail "go build failed"
+kind create cluster --name "$CLUSTER" --kubeconfig "$KUBECONFIG_FILE" --wait 120s >"$WORK/kind.log" 2>&1 || fail "kind create cluster failed: $(tail -n 3 "$WORK/kind.log")"
+
+REPO="$WORK/repo"
+mkdir -p "$REPO"
+git -C "$REPO" init -q -b master
+cm() { printf 'apiVersion: v1\nkind: ConfigMap\nmetadata:\n  name: %s\n  namespace: default\ndata:\n  key: v1\n' "$1"; }
+cm keep > "$REPO/keep.yaml"
+cm drop > "$REPO/drop.yaml"
+git -C "$REPO" -c user.name=verify -c user.email=verify@example.com add -A
+git -C "$REPO" -c user.name=verify -c user.email=verify@example.com commit -q -m init
+
+mkdir -p "$WORK/run/configs"
+cat > "$WORK/run/configs/clusters.json" <<JSON
+[{"name":"kind","kubeconfig_path":"$KUBECONFIG_FILE","registered_at":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}]
+JSON
+cat > "$WORK/run/configs/applications.json" <<JSON
+[{"name":"web","repo_url":"$REPO","branch":"master","path":".","cluster_name":"kind","interval":"2s","status":"Pending","prune":true}]
+JSON
+
+(cd "$WORK/run" && exec "$WORK/gitopsctl" start --api-address "127.0.0.1:$PORT" >"$WORK/controller.log" 2>&1) &
+PID=$!
+
+wait_for "controller health" 30 curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health"
+wait_for "app synced" 90 app_synced
+
+kc get configmap keep drop -n default >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "ConfigMaps were not created"
+labels="$(kc get configmap keep -n default -o json | jq -r '.metadata.labels | [.["app.kubernetes.io/managed-by"], .["gitopsctl.io/app"], .["gitopsctl.io/cluster"]] | join(",")')"
+[[ "$labels" == "gitopsctl,web,kind" ]] || fail "unexpected ownership labels: $labels"
+
+plan="$(cd "$WORK/run" && "$WORK/gitopsctl" --api-url "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT" diff-app -n web 2>&1)"
+grep -q "0 to create, 0 to update" <<<"$plan" || fail "diff-app does not report an in-sync app: $plan"
+
+rm "$REPO/drop.yaml"
+git -C "$REPO" -c user.name=verify -c user.email=verify@example.com commit -q -am "drop"
+wait_for "drop pruned" 90 bash -c "! kubectl --kubeconfig '$KUBECONFIG_FILE' get configmap drop -n default"
+kc get configmap keep -n default >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "prune removed a resource that is still in Git"
+
+echo "RESULT $ID PASS applied with ownership labels, diff clean, pruned only the removed resource"

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..23a3bab
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.verify/integration/fakekube_test.go
@@ -0,0 +1,225 @@
+package integration
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"fmt"
+	"io"
+	"net/http"
+	"net/http/httptest"
+	"strings"
+	"sync"
+	"testing"
+)
+
+type fakeKube struct {
+	srv *httptest.Server
+
+	mu        sync.Mutex
+	objects   map[string]map[string]any
+	mutations int
+	failWhen  func(method, name string) bool
+}
+
+func newFakeKube(t *testing.T) *fakeKube {
+	t.Helper()
+	k := &fakeKube{objects: map[string]map[string]any{}}
+	k.srv = httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(k.serve))
+	t.Cleanup(k.srv.Close)
+	return k
+}
+
+func (k *fakeKube) URL() string { return k.srv.URL }
+
+func (k *fakeKube) failMutationsWhen(fn func(method, name string) bool) {
+	k.mu.Lock()
+	defer k.mu.Unlock()
+	k.failWhen = fn
+}
+
+func (k *fakeKube) Mutations() int {
+	k.mu.Lock()
+	defer k.mu.Unlock()
+	return k.mutations
+}
+
+func (k *fakeKube) Get(namespace, name string) (map[string]any, bool) {
+	k.mu.Lock()
+	defer k.mu.Unlock()
+	obj, ok := k.objects[namespace+"/"+name]
+	if !ok {
+		return nil, false
+	}
+	return cloneJSON(obj), true
+}
+
+func (k *fakeKube) Seed(namespace, name string, labels map[string]string, data map[string]string) {
+	k.mu.Lock()
+	defer k.mu.Unlock()
+	k.objects[namespace+"/"+name] = configMap(namespace, name, labels, data)
+}
+
+func (k *fakeKube) Names() []string {
+	k.mu.Lock()
+	defer k.mu.Unlock()
+	names := make([]string, 0, len(k.objects))
+	for key := range k.objects {
+		names = append(names, key)
+	}
+	return names
+}
+
+func (k *fakeKube) Labels(namespace, name string) map[string]string {
+	obj, ok := k.Get(namespace, name)
+	if !ok {
+		return nil
+	}
+	labels := map[string]string{}
+	meta, _ := obj["metadata"].(map[string]any)
+	raw, _ := meta["labels"].(map[string]any)
+	for key, value := range raw {
+		labels[key], _ = value.(string)
+	}
+	return labels
+}
+
+func (k *fakeKube) DataValue(namespace, name, key string) string {
+	obj, ok := k.Get(namespace, name)
+	if !ok {
+		return ""
+	}
+	data, _ := obj["data"].(map[string]any)
+	value, _ := data[key].(string)
+	return value
+}
+
+func configMap(namespace, name string, labels map[string]string, data map[string]string) map[string]any {
+	meta := map[string]any{"name": name, "namespace": namespace, "resourceVersion": "1", "uid": "uid-" + name}
+	if len(labels) > 0 {
+		meta["labels"] = labels
+	}
+	obj := map[string]any{"apiVersion": "v1", "kind": "ConfigMap", "metadata": meta}
+	if len(data) > 0 {
+		obj["data"] = data
+	}
+	return obj
+}
+
+func cloneJSON(in map[string]any) map[string]any {
+	raw, _ := json.Marshal(in)
+	var out map[string]any
+	_ = json.Unmarshal(raw, &out)
+	return out
+}
+
+func writeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, body any) {
+	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
+	w.WriteHeader(status)
+	_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(body)
+}
+
+func writeStatus(w http.ResponseWriter, code int, reason, message string) {
+	writeJSON(w, code, map[string]any{
+		"kind": "Status", "apiVersion": "v1", "metadata": map[string]any{},
+		"status": "Failure", "message": message, "reason": reason, "code": code,
+	})
+}
+
+func (k *fakeKube) serve(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	switch r.URL.Path {
+	case "/version":
+		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"major": "1", "minor": "30", "gitVersion": "v1.30.0"})
+		return
+	case "/api":
+		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"kind": "APIVersions", "versions": []string{"v1"}})
+		return
+	case "/apis":
+		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"kind": "APIGroupList", "apiVersion": "v1", "groups": []any{}})
+		return
+	case "/api/v1":
+		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
+			"kind": "APIResourceList", "groupVersion": "v1",
+			"resources": []map[string]any{{
+				"name": "configmaps", "singularName": "configmap", "namespaced": true, "kind": "ConfigMap",
+				"verbs": []string{"create", "delete", "get", "list", "update"},
+			}},
+		})
+		return
+	}
+
+	parts := strings.Split(strings.Trim(r.URL.Path, "/"), "/")
+	if len(parts) < 5 || parts[0] != "api" || parts[1] != "v1" || parts[2] != "namespaces" || parts[4] != "configmaps" {
+		writeStatus(w, http.StatusNotFound, "NotFound", "unsupported path "+r.URL.Path)
+		return
+	}
+	namespace := parts[3]
+	name := ""
+	if len(parts) > 5 {
+		name = parts[5]
+	}
+	k.handleConfigMap(w, r, namespace, name)
+}
+
+func (k *fakeKube) handleConfigMap(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, namespace, name string) {
+	k.mu.Lock()
+	defer k.mu.Unlock()
+
+	mutating := r.Method == http.MethodPost || r.Method == http.MethodPut || r.Method == http.MethodDelete
+	var body map[string]any
+	if r.Method == http.MethodPost || r.Method == http.MethodPut {
+		raw, _ := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
+		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &body); err != nil {
+			writeStatus(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "BadRequest", err.Error())
+			return
+		}
+		if r.Method == http.MethodPost {
+			meta, _ := body["metadata"].(map[string]any)
+			name, _ = meta["name"].(string)
+		}
+	}
+
+	if mutating {
+		if k.failWhen != nil && k.failWhen(r.Method, name) {
+			writeStatus(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "InternalError", "injected failure")
+			return
+		}
+		k.mutations++
+	}
+
+	key := namespace + "/" + name
+	existing, exists := k.objects[key]
+	switch r.Method {
+	case http.MethodGet:
+		if !exists {
+			writeStatus(w, http.StatusNotFound, "NotFound", fmt.Sprintf("configmaps %q not found", name))
+			return
+		}
+		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, existing)
+	case http.MethodPost:
+		if exists {
+			writeStatus(w, http.StatusConflict, "AlreadyExists", "already exists")
+			return
+		}
+		meta, _ := body["metadata"].(map[string]any)
+		meta["namespace"], meta["resourceVersion"], meta["uid"] = namespace, "1", "uid-"+name
+		k.objects[key] = body
+		writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, body)
+	case http.MethodPut:
+		if !exists {
+			writeStatus(w, http.StatusNotFound, "NotFound", fmt.Sprintf("configmaps %q not found", name))
+			return
+		}
+		meta, _ := body["metadata"].(map[string]any)
+		meta["namespace"], meta["resourceVersion"] = namespace, "2"
+		k.objects[key] = body
+		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, body)
+	case http.MethodDelete:
+		if !exists {
+			writeStatus(w, http.StatusNotFound, "NotFound", fmt.Sprintf("configmaps %q not found", name))
+			return
+		}
+		delete(k.objects, key)
+		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"kind": "Status", "apiVersion": "v1", "status": "Success"})
+	default:
+		writeStatus(w, http.StatusMethodNotAllowed, "MethodNotAllowed", r.Method)
+	}
+}
diff --git a/.verify/integration/harness_test.go b/.verify/integration/harness_test.go
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..9e8ecd7
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.verify/integration/harness_test.go
@@ -0,0 +1,395 @@
+package integration
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"encoding/json"
+	"fmt"
+	"io"
+	"net"
+	"net/http"
+	"os"
+	"os/exec"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"strings"
+	"sync"
+	"syscall"
+	"testing"
+	"time"
+)
+
+var binaryPath string
+
+func TestMain(m *testing.M) {
+	dir, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "gitopsctl-verify-bin")
+	if err != nil {
+		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
+		os.Exit(1)
+	}
+	binaryPath = filepath.Join(dir, "gitopsctl")
+	build := exec.Command("go", "build", "-o", binaryPath, ".")
+	build.Dir = "../.."
+	if out, err := build.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
+		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "build failed: %v\n%s", err, out)
+		_ = os.RemoveAll(dir)
+		os.Exit(1)
+	}
+	code := m.Run()
+	_ = os.RemoveAll(dir)
+	os.Exit(code)
+}
+
+type syncBuffer struct {
+	mu  sync.Mutex
+	buf bytes.Buffer
+}
+
+func (b *syncBuffer) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
+	b.mu.Lock()
+	defer b.mu.Unlock()
+	return b.buf.Write(p)
+}
+
+func (b *syncBuffer) String() string {
+	b.mu.Lock()
+	defer b.mu.Unlock()
+	return b.buf.String()
+}
+
+type env struct {
+	t    *testing.T
+	root string
+	kube *fakeKube
+}
+
+func newEnv(t *testing.T) *env {
+	t.Helper()
+	root := t.TempDir()
+	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(root, "configs"), 0o755); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	return &env{t: t, root: root, kube: newFakeKube(t)}
+}
+
+func (e *env) configPath(name string) string { return filepath.Join(e.root, "configs", name) }
+
+func (e *env) run(args ...string) (string, int) {
+	e.t.Helper()
+	cmd := exec.Command(binaryPath, args...)
+	cmd.Dir = e.root
+	var out bytes.Buffer
+	cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &out, &out
+	err := cmd.Run()
+	if err == nil {
+		return out.String(), 0
+	}
+	if exitErr, ok := err.(*exec.ExitError); ok {
+		return out.String(), exitErr.ExitCode()
+	}
+	e.t.Fatalf("run %v: %v", args, err)
+	return "", -1
+}
+
+type proc struct {
+	cmd  *exec.Cmd
+	out  *syncBuffer
+	done chan struct{}
+	port int
+}
+
+func (p *proc) Output() string { return p.out.String() }
+
+func (p *proc) Alive() bool {
+	select {
+	case <-p.done:
+		return false
+	default:
+		return true
+	}
+}
+
+func (p *proc) ExitCode() int {
+	<-p.done
+	return p.cmd.ProcessState.ExitCode()
+}
+
+func (p *proc) WaitExit(timeout time.Duration) bool {
+	select {
+	case <-p.done:
+		return true
+	case <-time.After(timeout):
+		return false
+	}
+}
+
+func (p *proc) Stop() {
+	if !p.Alive() {
+		return
+	}
+	_ = p.cmd.Process.Signal(syscall.SIGTERM)
+	select {
+	case <-p.done:
+	case <-time.After(10 * time.Second):
+		_ = p.cmd.Process.Kill()
+		<-p.done
+	}
+}
+
+func freePort(t *testing.T) int {
+	t.Helper()
+	l, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	defer func() { _ = l.Close() }()
+	return l.Addr().(*net.TCPAddr).Port
+}
+
+func (e *env) startNoWait(args ...string) *proc {
+	e.t.Helper()
+	port := freePort(e.t)
+	return e.launch(port, append([]string{"start", "--api-address", fmt.Sprintf("127.0.0.1:%d", port)}, args...))
+}
+
+func (e *env) launch(port int, full []string) *proc {
+	e.t.Helper()
+	cmd := exec.Command(binaryPath, full...)
+	cmd.Dir = e.root
+	out := &syncBuffer{}
+	cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = out, out
+	if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
+		e.t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	p := &proc{cmd: cmd, out: out, done: make(chan struct{}), port: port}
+	go func() {
+		_ = cmd.Wait()
+		close(p.done)
+	}()
+	e.t.Cleanup(p.Stop)
+	return p
+}
+
+func (e *env) start(args ...string) *proc {
+	e.t.Helper()
+	p := e.startNoWait(args...)
+	deadline := time.Now().Add(20 * time.Second)
+	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
+		if !p.Alive() {
+			e.t.Fatalf("controller exited early:\n%s", p.Output())
+		}
+		resp, err := http.Get(p.url("/health"))
+		if err == nil {
+			_ = resp.Body.Close()
+			if resp.StatusCode == http.StatusOK {
+				return p
+			}
+		}
+		time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)
+	}
+	e.t.Fatalf("controller did not become healthy:\n%s", p.Output())
+	return nil
+}
+
+func (p *proc) url(path string) string { return fmt.Sprintf("http://127.0.0.1:%d%s", p.port, path) }
+
+func (p *proc) api(method, path, token string, body any) (int, []byte) {
+	var reader io.Reader
+	if body != nil {
+		raw, _ := json.Marshal(body)
+		reader = bytes.NewReader(raw)
+	}
+	req, err := http.NewRequest(method, p.url(path), reader)
+	if err != nil {
+		panic(err)
+	}
+	if body != nil {
+		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
+	}
+	if token != "" {
+		req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
+	}
+	resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
+	if err != nil {
+		return 0, []byte(err.Error())
+	}
+	defer func() { _ = resp.Body.Close() }()
+	data, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
+	return resp.StatusCode, data
+}
+
+func (p *proc) header(method, path, token, name string) string {
+	req, _ := http.NewRequest(method, p.url(path), nil)
+	if token != "" {
+		req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
+	}
+	resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
+	if err != nil {
+		return ""
+	}
+	defer func() { _ = resp.Body.Close() }()
+	return resp.Header.Get(name)
+}
+
+type appState struct {
+	Status       string `json:"status"`
+	Message      string `json:"message"`
+	LastSynced   string `json:"last_synced_git_hash"`
+	LatestHash   string `json:"latest_git_hash"`
+	Failures     int    `json:"consecutive_failures"`
+	SyncPolicy   string `json:"sync_policy"`
+	ApprovedHash string `json:"approved_git_hash"`
+	Prune        bool   `json:"prune"`
+}
+
+func (p *proc) appState(token, name string) (appState, bool) {
+	status, body := p.api(http.MethodGet, "/api/v1/applications/"+name, token, nil)
+	if status != http.StatusOK {
+		return appState{}, false
+	}
+	var st appState
+	if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &st); err != nil {
+		return appState{}, false
+	}
+	return st, true
+}
+
+func (e *env) waitFor(timeout time.Duration, desc string, cond func() bool) {
+	e.t.Helper()
+	deadline := time.Now().Add(timeout)
+	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
+		if cond() {
+			return
+		}
+		time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)
+	}
+	e.t.Fatalf("timed out after %s waiting for: %s", timeout, desc)
+}
+
+func (e *env) waitForApp(p *proc, token, name string, timeout time.Duration, desc string, pred func(appState) bool) appState {
+	e.t.Helper()
+	var last appState
+	e.waitFor(timeout, desc+fmt.Sprintf(" (app %s)", name), func() bool {
+		st, ok := p.appState(token, name)
+		last = st
+		return ok && pred(st)
+	})
+	return last
+}
+
+func (e *env) writeKubeconfig(path, server string) {
+	e.t.Helper()
+	content := fmt.Sprintf(`apiVersion: v1
+kind: Config
+clusters:
+- cluster:
+    server: %s
+  name: fake
+contexts:
+- context:
+    cluster: fake
+    user: fake
+  name: fake
+current-context: fake
+users:
+- name: fake
+  user: {}
+`, server)
+	if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(content), 0o600); err != nil {
+		e.t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+}
+
+func (e *env) writeJSON(path string, v any) {
+	e.t.Helper()
+	raw, err := json.MarshalIndent(v, "", "  ")
+	if err != nil {
+		e.t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if err := os.WriteFile(path, raw, 0o644); err != nil {
+		e.t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+}
+
+func (e *env) useFakeCluster(name string, allowedNamespaces ...string) {
+	e.t.Helper()
+	kubeconfig := filepath.Join(e.root, "kubeconfig.yaml")
+	e.writeKubeconfig(kubeconfig, e.kube.URL())
+	cluster := map[string]any{"name": name, "kubeconfig_path": kubeconfig, "registered_at": time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339)}
+	if len(allowedNamespaces) > 0 {
+		cluster["allowed_namespaces"] = allowedNamespaces
+	}
+	e.writeJSON(e.configPath("clusters.json"), []any{cluster})
+}
+
+func (e *env) writeApps(apps ...map[string]any) {
+	e.t.Helper()
+	list := make([]any, 0, len(apps))
+	for _, app := range apps {
+		list = append(list, app)
+	}
+	e.writeJSON(e.configPath("applications.json"), list)
+}
+
+func appSpec(name, repo string, extra map[string]any) map[string]any {
+	app := map[string]any{
+		"name": name, "repo_url": repo, "branch": "master", "path": ".",
+		"cluster_name": "c1", "interval": "1s", "status": "Pending",
+	}
+	for key, value := range extra {
+		app[key] = value
+	}
+	return app
+}
+
+func manifest(name, value string) string {
+	return fmt.Sprintf("apiVersion: v1\nkind: ConfigMap\nmetadata:\n  name: %s\ndata:\n  key: %s\n", name, value)
+}
+
+func manifestIn(namespace, name, value string) string {
+	return fmt.Sprintf("apiVersion: v1\nkind: ConfigMap\nmetadata:\n  name: %s\n  namespace: %s\ndata:\n  key: %s\n", name, namespace, value)
+}
+
+func git(t *testing.T, dir string, args ...string) string {
+	t.Helper()
+	cmd := exec.Command("git", append([]string{"-c", "user.name=verify", "-c", "user.email=verify@example.com", "-c", "commit.gpgsign=false"}, args...)...)
+	cmd.Dir = dir
+	out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("git %v: %v\n%s", args, err, out)
+	}
+	return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
+}
+
+func newRepo(t *testing.T, files map[string]string) string {
+	t.Helper()
+	dir := t.TempDir()
+	git(t, dir, "init", "-b", "master")
+	commitFiles(t, dir, files, nil)
+	return dir
+}
+
+func commitFiles(t *testing.T, repo string, write map[string]string, remove []string) string {
+	t.Helper()
+	for name, content := range write {
+		path := filepath.Join(repo, name)
+		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(content), 0o644); err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+	}
+	for _, name := range remove {
+		if err := os.Remove(filepath.Join(repo, name)); err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+	}
+	git(t, repo, "add", "-A")
+	git(t, repo, "commit", "-m", "change", "--allow-empty")
+	return git(t, repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
+}
+
+const (
+	managedByLabel = "app.kubernetes.io/managed-by"
+	appLabel       = "gitopsctl.io/app"
+	clusterLabel   = "gitopsctl.io/cluster"
+)

+		if out, code := e.run(append([]string{"register-cluster"}, args...)...); code == 0 {
+			t.Errorf("%s: expected failure, got success:\n%s", name, out)
+		}
+	}
+	if clusters := readList(t, e.configPath("clusters.json")); len(clusters) != 0 {
+		t.Fatalf("rejected registrations persisted state: %v", clusters)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestScenario_S_DOC_01_ExamplesLoadAndFlagsAreDocumented(t *testing.T) {
+	e := newEnv(t)
+	for src, dst := range map[string]string{"examples/configs/apps.json": "applications.json", "examples/configs/clusters.json": "clusters.json"} {
+		if err := os.WriteFile(e.configPath(dst), []byte(repoFile(t, src)), 0o644); err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+	}
+	out, code := e.run("list-apps")
+	if code != 0 || !strings.Contains(out, "nginx-demo") || !strings.Contains(out, "github.com/aeswibon") || !strings.Contains(out, "local-dev") {
+		t.Fatalf("example application config does not load into usable state (exit %d):\n%s", code, out)
+	}
+	out, code = e.run("list-clusters")
+	if code != 0 || !strings.Contains(out, "local-dev") {
+		t.Fatalf("example cluster config does not load (exit %d):\n%s", code, out)
+	}
+
+	docs := repoFile(t, "docs/cli-reference.md") + repoFile(t, "docs/configuration.md")
+	help, _ := e.run("start", "--help")
+	for _, flag := range regexp.MustCompile(`--[a-z][a-z-]+`).FindAllString(help, -1) {
+		if flag == "--help" {
+			continue
+		}
+		if !strings.Contains(docs, flag) {
+			t.Errorf("flag %s of `start` is not documented in docs/", flag)
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+func TestScenario_S_REL_01_ReleaseSupplyChainIsHardened(t *testing.T) {
+	if !strings.Contains(repoFile(t, "LICENSE"), "Apache License") {
+		t.Error("LICENSE is missing or not Apache-2.0")
+	}
+
+	goreleaser := repoFile(t, ".goreleaser.yaml")
+	for _, key := range []string{"checksum:", "sboms:", "signs:", "docker_signs:"} {
+		if !strings.Contains(goreleaser, key) {
+			t.Errorf(".goreleaser.yaml lacks %s", key)
+		}
+	}
+	if !regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^FROM \S+@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}`).MatchString(repoFile(t, "Dockerfile")) {
+		t.Error("Dockerfile base image is not pinned by digest")
+	}
+
+	goVersion := regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^go (\S+)$`).FindStringSubmatch(repoFile(t, "go.mod"))
+	workflows, _ := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join("..", "..", ".github", "workflows", "*.yml"))
+	if goVersion == nil || len(workflows) == 0 {
+		t.Fatal("cannot find go.mod version or workflows")
+	}
+	pinned := regexp.MustCompile(`uses:\s+\S+@[0-9a-f]{40}\s*$`)
+	for _, workflow := range workflows {
+		raw, _ := os.ReadFile(workflow)
+		for _, line := range strings.Split(string(raw), "\n") {
+			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
+			if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "uses:") && !pinned.MatchString(trimmed) {
+				t.Errorf("%s: action not pinned by SHA: %s", filepath.Base(workflow), trimmed)
+			}
+			if strings.Contains(trimmed, "go-version:") && !strings.Contains(trimmed, `"`+goVersion[1]+`"`) {
+				t.Errorf("%s: %s does not match go.mod (%s)", filepath.Base(workflow), trimmed, goVersion[1])
+			}
+			if strings.Contains(trimmed, "@latest") || trimmed == "version: latest" {
+				t.Errorf("%s: unpinned tool version: %s", filepath.Base(workflow), trimmed)
+			}
+		}
+	}
+}

+package integration

+func pruneFiles(names ...string) map[string]string {

+	for _, name := range names {
+		files[name+".yaml"] = manifest(name, "v1")
+	}
+	return files
+}
+
+func exists(e *env, name string) bool {
+	_, ok := e.kube.Get("default", name)
+	return ok
+}
+
+func TestScenario_S_PRUNE_01_RemovedManifestsAreDeletedWhenPruneIsEnabled(t *testing.T) {
+	e, p, repo := syncedEnv(t, pruneFiles("keep", "drop"), map[string]any{"prune": true})
+	e.waitForApp(p, "", "web", settle, "initial sync", isSynced)
+	e.kube.Seed("default", "bystander", map[string]string{managedByLabel: "gitopsctl", appLabel: "another-app"}, nil)
+
+	head := commitFiles(t, repo, nil, []string{"drop.yaml"})
+	e.waitForApp(p, "", "web", settle, "prune synced", func(st appState) bool { return isSynced(st) && st.LastSynced == head })
+	e.waitFor(settle, "pruned resource deleted", func() bool { return !exists(e, "drop") })
+
+	if !exists(e, "keep") || !exists(e, "bystander") {
+		t.Fatalf("prune removed the wrong resources: %v", e.kube.Names())
+	}
+}

+func TestScenario_S_PRUNE_02_RemovedManifestsStayWhenPruneIsDisabled(t *testing.T) {
+	e, p, repo := syncedEnv(t, pruneFiles("keep", "drop"), nil)
+	e.waitForApp(p, "", "web", settle, "initial sync", isSynced)
+
+	head := commitFiles(t, repo, nil, []string{"drop.yaml"})
+	e.waitForApp(p, "", "web", settle, "second sync", func(st appState) bool { return isSynced(st) && st.LastSynced == head })
+
+	if !exists(e, "drop") || !exists(e, "keep") {
+		t.Fatalf("resources were deleted although prune is off: %v", e.kube.Names())
+	}

+func TestScenario_F_PRUNE_01_ResourcesNotOwnedByTheAppSurvivePruning(t *testing.T) {

+	head := commitFiles(t, repo, nil, []string{"drop.yaml"})
+	e.waitForApp(p, "", "web", settle, "sync after removal", func(st appState) bool { return isSynced(st) && st.LastSynced == head })

diff --git a/.verify/run.sh b/.verify/run.sh
new file mode 100755
index 0000000..887fbe0
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.verify/run.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,211 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Runs the quality gates and success/failure scenarios defined in .verify/scenarios.json
+# and writes a scored report to .verify/report.json.
+#
+# Usage: .verify/run.sh [--no-gates] [--no-scenarios] [--no-e2e] [--only ID[,ID...]] [--list]
+# Exit status: 0 = PASS, 1 = CONDITIONAL or FAIL, 2 = harness error.
+set -uo pipefail
+
+HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)"
+CATALOG="$HERE/scenarios.json"
+WORK="$HERE/.work"
+REPORT="$HERE/report.json"
+RUN_GATES=1
+RUN_SCENARIOS=1
+RUN_E2E=1
+ONLY=""
+
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --no-gates) RUN_GATES=0 ;;
+    --no-scenarios) RUN_SCENARIOS=0 ;;
+    --no-e2e) RUN_E2E=0 ;;
+    --only) ONLY="${2:-}"; shift ;;
+    --list)
+      jq -r '(.gates[] | [.id, "gate", .severity, .title]), (.scenarios[] | [.id, .kind, .severity, .title]) | @tsv' "$CATALOG"
+      exit 0 ;;
+    -h|--help) sed -n '2,6p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "unknown argument: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+  shift
+done
+
+for tool in jq go git; do
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "required tool missing: $tool" >&2; exit 2; }
+done
+
+cd "$ROOT"
+rm -rf "$WORK"
+mkdir -p "$WORK"
+RESULTS="$WORK/results.jsonl"
+: > "$RESULTS"
+MODULE="$(go list -m)"
+
+record() {
+  jq -cn --arg id "$1" --arg kind "$2" --arg severity "$3" --arg title "$4" --arg status "$5" \
+    --argjson duration "$6" --arg detail "$7" \
+    '{id:$id, kind:$kind, severity:$severity, title:$title, status:$status, duration_s:$duration, detail:$detail}' >> "$RESULTS"
+}
+
+tail_of() { tail -n "${2:-20}" "$1" | tail -c 2000; }
+
+run_gates() {
+  while IFS= read -r gate; do
+    id="$(jq -r .id <<<"$gate")"
+    title="$(jq -r .title <<<"$gate")"
+    severity="$(jq -r .severity <<<"$gate")"
+    command="$(jq -r .command <<<"$gate")"
+    skip_tool="$(jq -r '.skip_if_missing // empty' <<<"$gate")"
+    threshold="$(jq -r '.threshold // empty' <<<"$gate")"
+
+    if [[ -n "$skip_tool" ]] && ! command -v "$skip_tool" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      record "$id" gate "$severity" "$title" skipped 0 "$skip_tool is not installed"
+      continue
+    fi
+
+    echo "[gate] $id: $title" >&2
+    started=$(date +%s)
+    if [[ "$command" == "coverage" ]]; then
+      if [[ ! -s "$WORK/cover.out" ]]; then
+        record "$id" gate "$severity" "$title" skipped 0 "no coverage profile (G-UNIT did not produce one)"
+        continue
+      fi
+      total="$(go tool cover -func="$WORK/cover.out" | awk '/^total:/ {gsub("%","",$3); print $3}')"
+      elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - started ))
+      if awk -v t="$total" -v th="$threshold" 'BEGIN{exit !(t+0 >= th+0)}'; then
+        record "$id" gate "$severity" "$title" pass "$elapsed" "total coverage ${total}% (threshold ${threshold}%)"
+      else
+        record "$id" gate "$severity" "$title" fail "$elapsed" "total coverage ${total}% is below ${threshold}%"
+      fi
+      continue
+    fi
+
+    bash -c "$command" > "$WORK/$id.log" 2>&1
+    code=$?
+    elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - started ))
+    if [[ $code -eq 0 ]]; then
+      record "$id" gate "$severity" "$title" pass "$elapsed" ""
+    else
+      record "$id" gate "$severity" "$title" fail "$elapsed" "exit $code: $(tail_of "$WORK/$id.log" 25)"
+    fi
+  done < <(jq -c '.gates[]' "$CATALOG")
+}
+
+run_go_scenarios() {
+  idx=0
+  while IFS=$'\t' read -r pkg race tests; do
+    idx=$((idx + 1))
+    echo "[tests] $pkg ($(tr '|' ' ' <<<"$tests" | wc -w | tr -d ' ') tests)" >&2
+    args=(test -json -count=1)
+    [[ "$race" == "true" ]] && args+=(-race)
+    go "${args[@]}" -run "^(${tests})\$" "$pkg" > "$WORK/go-$idx.json" 2>&1
+  done < <(jq -r --arg only "$ONLY" '
+    [.scenarios[] | select(.verify.type=="go-test") | select($only=="" or (.id as $sid | $only|split(",")|index($sid)))
+      | .verify as $v | $v.targets[] | {package, race: ($v.race // false), tests}]
+    | group_by([.package, .race])[]
+    | [.[0].package, (.[0].race|tostring), ([.[].tests[]] | unique | join("|"))] | @tsv' "$CATALOG")
+
+  cat "$WORK"/go-*.json 2>/dev/null | jq -R -s -c 'split("\n") | map(fromjson?)' > "$WORK/events.json"
+  [[ -s "$WORK/events.json" ]] || echo '[]' > "$WORK/events.json"
+
+  jq -c --slurpfile ev "$WORK/events.json" --arg m "$MODULE" --arg only "$ONLY" '
+    def pkgpath: if startswith("./") then $m + "/" + .[2:] else . end;
+    ($ev[0]) as $events
+    | ($events | map(select(.Test != null and (.Test | contains("/") | not)))) as $tests
+    | ($tests | map(select(.Action=="pass" or .Action=="fail" or .Action=="skip")) | map({key: (.Package + "|" + .Test), value: .Action}) | from_entries) as $res
+    | ($tests | map(select(.Action=="output")) | group_by(.Package + "|" + .Test)
+        | map({key: (.[0].Package + "|" + .[0].Test), value: (map(.Output) | join("") | .[-1200:])}) | from_entries) as $out
+    | ($events | map(select(.Test == null and .Action=="output")) | group_by(.Package)
+        | map({key: .[0].Package, value: (map(.Output) | join("") | .[-800:])}) | from_entries) as $pkgout
+    | .scenarios[] | select(.verify.type=="go-test") | select($only=="" or (.id as $sid | $only|split(",")|index($sid)))
+    | . as $s
+    | [$s.verify.targets[] | (.package | pkgpath) as $p | .tests[] | {test: ., pkg: $p, key: ($p + "|" + .)}] as $checks
+    | ($checks | map(. + {result: ($res[.key] // "missing")})) as $r
+    | {id, kind, severity, title,
+       status: (if all($r[]; .result=="pass") then "pass" else "fail" end),
+       duration_s: 0,
+       detail: ($r | map(select(.result != "pass"))
+                 | map("\(.test): \(.result)\n" + (if .result=="missing" then ($pkgout[.pkg] // "") else ($out[.key] // "") end))
+                 | join("\n"))}' "$CATALOG" >> "$RESULTS"
+}
+
+run_e2e() {
+  while IFS= read -r scenario; do
+    id="$(jq -r .id <<<"$scenario")"
+    title="$(jq -r .title <<<"$scenario")"
+    severity="$(jq -r .severity <<<"$scenario")"
+    script="$(jq -r .verify.script <<<"$scenario")"
+    missing=""
+    for tool in $(jq -r '.verify.skip_if_missing[]?' <<<"$scenario"); do
+      command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing="$missing $tool"
+    done
+    if [[ -z "$missing" ]] && command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      missing=" docker daemon"
+    fi
+    if [[ $RUN_E2E -eq 0 ]]; then
+      record "$id" "$(jq -r .kind <<<"$scenario")" "$severity" "$title" skipped 0 "--no-e2e"
+      continue
+    fi
+    if [[ -n "$missing" ]]; then
+      record "$id" "$(jq -r .kind <<<"$scenario")" "$severity" "$title" skipped 0 "unavailable:${missing}"
+      continue
+    fi
+    echo "[e2e] $id via $script" >&2
+    bash "$ROOT/$script" > "$WORK/$id.log" 2>&1
+    line="$(grep -E "^RESULT $id " "$WORK/$id.log" | tail -n 1)"
+    verdict="$(awk '{print $3}' <<<"$line")"
+    detail="$(cut -d' ' -f4- <<<"$line")"
+    case "$verdict" in
+      PASS) record "$id" "$(jq -r .kind <<<"$scenario")" "$severity" "$title" pass 0 "$detail" ;;
+      SKIP) record "$id" "$(jq -r .kind <<<"$scenario")" "$severity" "$title" skipped 0 "$detail" ;;
+      *) record "$id" "$(jq -r .kind <<<"$scenario")" "$severity" "$title" fail 0 "${detail:-no RESULT line}: $(tail_of "$WORK/$id.log" 20)" ;;
+    esac
+  done < <(jq -c --arg only "$ONLY" '.scenarios[] | select(.verify.type=="e2e") | select($only=="" or (.id as $sid | $only|split(",")|index($sid)))' "$CATALOG")
+}
+
+[[ $RUN_GATES -eq 1 && -z "$ONLY" ]] && run_gates
+if [[ $RUN_SCENARIOS -eq 1 ]]; then
+  run_go_scenarios
+  run_e2e
+fi
+
+jq -s --slurpfile catalog "$CATALOG" \
+   --arg commit "$(git rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)" \
+   --arg branch "$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)" \
+   --arg dirty "$(git status --porcelain 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^?? .verify/' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" \
+   --arg now "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" '
+  . as $results
+  | $catalog[0].severity_weights as $w
+  | ($results | map(select(.status != "skipped"))) as $scored
+  | ($scored | map($w[.severity]) | add // 0) as $total
+  | ($scored | map(select(.status=="pass") | $w[.severity]) | add // 0) as $earned
+  | (if $total == 0 then 0 else (($earned * 10000 / $total) | round / 100) end) as $score
+  | ($results | map(select(.status=="fail"))) as $failed
+  | ($failed | map(select(.severity=="critical" or .severity=="high")) | map(.id)) as $blocking
+  | ($failed | map(select(.severity=="critical")) | map(.id)) as $critical
+  | {
+      generated_at: $now,
+      git: {commit: $commit, branch: $branch, uncommitted_files: ($dirty | tonumber)},
+      summary: {
+        total: ($results | length),
+        passed: ($results | map(select(.status=="pass")) | length),
+        failed: ($failed | length),
+        skipped: ($results | map(select(.status=="skipped")) | length),
+        score: $score,
+        verdict: (if ($blocking | length) == 0 and $score >= 95 then "PASS"
+                  elif ($critical | length) == 0 and $score >= 80 then "CONDITIONAL"
+                  else "FAIL" end),
+        blocking_failures: $blocking
+      },
+      results: $results
+    }' "$RESULTS" > "$REPORT"
+
+jq -r '
+  "VERDICT \(.summary.verdict)  score \(.summary.score)  pass \(.summary.passed)  fail \(.summary.failed)  skipped \(.summary.skipped)",
+  (.results[] | "\(.status | ascii_upcase | .[0:4])  \(.id)  [\(.severity)]  \(.title)" + (if .status != "pass" and .detail != "" then "\n      " + (.detail | split("\n")[0:6] | join("\n      ")) else "" end))
+' "$REPORT"
+echo "report: $REPORT"
+
+verdict="$(jq -r .summary.verdict "$REPORT")"
+[[ "$verdict" == "PASS" ]]

+# Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct
+
+## Our Pledge
+
+We as members, contributors, and leaders pledge to make participation in our
+community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body
+size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender
+identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status,
+nationality, personal appearance, race, caste, color, religion, or sexual
+identity and orientation.
+
+We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming,
+diverse, inclusive, and healthy community.
+
+## Our Standards
+
+Examples of behavior that contributes to a positive environment for our
+community include:
+
+* Demonstrating empathy and kindness toward other people
+* Being respectful of differing opinions, viewpoints, and experiences
+* Giving and gracefully accepting constructive feedback
+* Accepting responsibility and apologizing to those affected by our mistakes,
+  and learning from the experience
+* Focusing on what is best not just for us as individuals, but for the overall
+  community
+
+Examples of unacceptable behavior include:
+
+* The use of sexualized language or imagery, and sexual attention or advances of
+  any kind
+* Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks
+* Public or private harassment
+* Publishing others' private information, such as a physical or email address,
+  without their explicit permission
+* Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a
+  professional setting
+
+## Enforcement Responsibilities
+
+Community leaders are responsible for clarifying and enforcing our standards of
+acceptable behavior and will take appropriate and fair corrective action in
+response to any behavior that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive,
+or harmful.
+
+Community leaders have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject
+comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions that are
+not aligned to this Code of Conduct, and will communicate reasons for moderation
+decisions when appropriate.
+
+## Scope
+
+This Code of Conduct applies within all community spaces, and also applies when
+an individual is officially representing the community in public spaces.
+Examples of representing our community include using an official e-mail address,
+posting via an official social media account, or acting as an appointed
+representative at an online or offline event.
+
+## Enforcement
+
+Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be
+reported to the community leaders responsible for enforcement by opening an issue
+or contacting the repository owner. All complaints will be reviewed and
+investigated promptly and fairly.
+
+All community leaders are obligated to respect the privacy and security of the
+reporter of any incident.
+
+## Attribution
+
+This Code of Conduct is adapted from the [Contributor Covenant][homepage],
+version 2.1, available at
+[https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html][v2.1].
+
+[homepage]: https://www.contributor-covenant.org
+[v2.1]: https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html

+# Contributing to GitOpsCTL
+
+First off, thank you for considering contributing to GitOpsCTL! It's people like you that make GitOpsCTL such a great tool.
+
+## Getting Started
+
+### Prerequisites
+
+- **Go 1.24+**: Ensure you have Go installed and matching the `go.mod` version.
+- **Git**: For version control.
+- **Kubernetes Cluster**: A running cluster (e.g., OrbStack, minikube, kind, or Docker Desktop) to test changes locally.
+
+### Local Development Setup
+
+1. **Fork the repository** on GitHub.
+2. **Clone your fork** locally:
+   ```bash
+   git clone https://github.com/your-username/gitopsctl.git
+   cd gitopsctl
+   ```
+3. **Install dependencies**:
+   ```bash
+   go mod tidy
+   ```
+4. **Build the CLI**:
+   ```bash
+   go build -o gitopsctl .
+   ```
+5. **Set up hooks**:
+   We use `pre-commit` to ensure code quality. Coverage checks are enforced on push.
+   ```bash
+   pip install pre-commit
+   pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type pre-push
+   ```
+6. **Run tests & check coverage**:
+   ```bash
+   go test -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...
+   go tool cover -func=coverage.out
+   ```
+   Then run the success/failure scenarios in `.verify/` (needs `jq`); see `.verify/README.md`:
+   ```bash
+   .verify/run.sh --no-e2e
+   ```
+
+
+
+## How to Contribute
+
+### 1. Find an Issue
+Look for issues labeled `good first issue` or `help wanted` if you're not sure where to start. If you want to work on something specific, it's best to open an issue first to discuss it before spending time writing code.
+
+### 2. Create a Branch
+Create a branch for your feature or bug fix:
+```bash
+git checkout -b feature/my-awesome-feature
+```
+
+### 3. Make Changes
+Write your code, making sure to follow standard Go conventions.
+- Run `go fmt ./...` to format your code.
+- Run `go vet ./...` to catch common mistakes.
+- **Maintain Test Coverage**: Ensure all changes are covered by tests. The project enforces a minimum of **80% total coverage**.
+- Ensure all existing and new tests pass.
+
+
+### 4. Commit Messages
+Write clear, concise commit messages. A good commit message should describe *what* was changed and *why*.
+```text
+feat(api): add a new endpoint for fetching logs
+
+This adds a new `/api/v1/logs` endpoint to support the new dashboard UI.
+Fixes #123
+```
+
+### 5. Submit a Pull Request
+Push your branch to your fork and submit a Pull Request against the `main` branch of the upstream repository.
+- Fill out the PR template completely.
+- Ensure CI checks pass.
+- Be responsive to feedback from reviewers.
+
+## Documentation
+If your change introduces new features, make sure to update the relevant documentation in the `docs/` folder or the `README.md`.
+
+Thank you for your contributions!

+# Build stage is handled by GoReleaser
+FROM alpine:3.21@sha256:ce64758a109eb420d874a118f87920e625e12d3634e03b4a5573fd9f6e5d3507
+
+RUN apk add --no-cache ca-certificates git openssh tzdata
+
+# Create a non-root user
+RUN addgroup -S gitopsctl && adduser -S gitopsctl -G gitopsctl
+USER gitopsctl
+
+WORKDIR /app
+
+# GoReleaser will copy the built binary into the image
+ARG TARGETPLATFORM
+COPY ${TARGETPLATFORM}/gitopsctl /usr/local/bin/gitopsctl
+
+ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/gitopsctl"]
+CMD ["start"]

+# GitOpsCTL
+
+<p align="center">
+  <img src="assets/logo.png" alt="GitOpsCTL Logo" width="200" />
+</p>
+
+[![Build Status](https://github.com/aeswibon/gitopsctl/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/aeswibon/gitopsctl/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
+[![Go Report Card](https://goreportcard.com/badge/github.com/aeswibon/gitopsctl)](https://goreportcard.com/report/github.com/aeswibon/gitopsctl)
+
+GitOpsCTL is a lightweight, external GitOps control plane for Kubernetes. It watches Git repositories, renders plain YAML, Kustomize, or Helm manifests, applies them to registered clusters, and exposes a CLI, REST API, Server-Sent Events stream, Prometheus metrics, JSONL event log, webhooks, and an interactive terminal dashboard.
+
+Unlike in-cluster GitOps controllers, GitOpsCTL can run from a laptop, CI runner, bastion host, management VM, or container while managing one or more remote Kubernetes clusters through kubeconfig files.
+
+## What It Does
+
+- Watches application Git repositories on a configurable interval.
+- Applies raw Kubernetes YAML, Kustomize overlays, or Helm charts.
+- Supports automatic sync and manual approval workflows.
+- Manages multiple clusters from one controller process.
+- Restricts cluster writes to configured namespaces when `allowed_namespaces` is set.
+- Decrypts SOPS-encrypted YAML, YML, and JSON manifests before apply.
+- Tracks app and cluster status in local JSON config files.
+- Exposes an API and TUI for operational commands and live status.
+- Emits integration events to SSE, JSONL files, and HTTP webhooks.
+- Publishes Prometheus metrics for syncs, cluster health, app health, Git pulls, and Kubernetes applies.
+
+## Quick Start
+
+Prerequisites:
+
+- A Kubernetes cluster reachable through `kubectl`.
+- A kubeconfig file for that cluster.
+- GitOpsCTL installed. See [Installation](docs/installation.md).
+
+```bash
+# 1. Register a cluster.
+gitopsctl register-cluster \
+  --name local-dev \
+  --kubeconfig ~/.kube/config \
+  --allowed-namespaces demo
+
+# 2. Register the example nginx app.
+gitopsctl register-apps \
+  --name nginx-demo \
+  --repo https://github.com/aeswibon/gitopsctl.git \
+  --branch main \
+  --path examples/manifests \
+  --cluster local-dev \
+  --interval 30s \
+  --sync-policy auto
+
+# 3. Start the controller and API server.
+gitopsctl start --api-address :8080
+
+# 4. In another terminal, open the dashboard.
+gitopsctl dashboard --api-url http://127.0.0.1:8080
+```
+
+To start from checked-in sample config files instead of registering resources manually, see [Examples](examples/README.md).
+
+## Documentation
+
+- [Getting Started](docs/getting-started.md): First local sync, dashboard, status checks, and cleanup.
+- [Installation](docs/installation.md): Install from releases, Go, Docker, or source.
+- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md): Complete `applications.json` and `clusters.json` reference.
+- [CLI Reference](docs/cli-reference.md): Commands, flags, and common workflows.
+- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): Controller, API, event bus, reconciliation, and storage model.
+- [Terminal Dashboard](docs/features/tui.md): TUI views and keyboard controls.
+- [Security](docs/features/security.md): Kubeconfig hygiene, namespace restrictions, RBAC, and SOPS.
+- [SOPS](docs/SOPS.md): Secret encryption and decryption setup.
+- [Observability](docs/features/observability.md): Metrics, events, JSONL audit logs, webhooks, and SSE.
+- [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md): Common setup and runtime failures.
+
+## Repository Layout
+
+```text
+cmd/                    Cobra CLI commands
+internal/api/           REST API, SSE stream, metrics endpoint
+internal/controller/    Reconciliation loop and command dispatch
+internal/core/app/      Application model and persistence
+internal/core/cluster/  Cluster model and persistence
+internal/core/git/      Git clone, pull, and commit helpers
+internal/core/k8s/      Kubernetes client, render, apply, health logic
+internal/events/        Event bus, history, stream, file, webhook sinks
+internal/tui/           Bubble Tea terminal dashboard
+docs/                   User and architecture documentation
+examples/               Runnable sample configs and manifests
+configs/                Default local runtime config directory
+```
+
+## Development
+
+```bash
+go test ./...
+go test ./... -coverprofile=coverage.out
+go tool cover -func=coverage.out
+```
+
+The project expects tests for new behavior and keeps coverage high across core packages.
+
+## Contributing
+
+Contributions are welcome. Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), run the test suite, and keep docs updated when changing commands, flags, config fields, or user-visible behavior.
+
+## License
+
+GitOpsCTL is licensed under the Apache License 2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

+# Security Policy
+
+## Supported Versions
+
+Currently, GitOpsCTL is in early development. Only the `main` branch and the latest release tag are actively supported with security updates.
+
+## Reporting a Vulnerability
+
+Security is taken very seriously. If you discover a security vulnerability within GitOpsCTL, please do **not** open a public issue.
+
+Instead, please report it via one of the following methods:
+
+1. **GitHub Security Advisories**: If enabled on this repository, you can privately report a vulnerability by going to the **Security** tab, clicking **Advisories**, and selecting **Report a vulnerability**.
+2. **Direct Contact**: If GitHub Security Advisories are not available, please contact the repository owner directly via the contact information provided in their GitHub profile.
+
+We will review all reports and do our best to acknowledge the issue within 48 hours and provide a timeline for a fix.
+
+### What to include in your report
+
+Please include as much detail as possible to help us reproduce and fix the issue quickly:
+- Description of the vulnerability.
+- Steps to reproduce.
+- Potential impact.
+- Any suggested mitigations.
+
+Thank you for helping keep GitOpsCTL secure!

+package cmd
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"net/url"
+
+	"aeswibon.com/github/gitopsctl/internal/events"
+	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
+)
+
+var (
+	approveAppName    string
+	approveCommitHash string
+)
+
+var approveAppCmd = &cobra.Command{
+	Use:     "approve-app",
+	GroupID: "appGroup",
+	Short:   "Approve a pending sync for an application (via controller API)",
+	Long: `Sends an HTTP request to a running gitopsctl controller to approve a specific commit for an application.
+This is used when the application's sync policy is set to 'manual'.`,
+	Example: `
+  gitopsctl approve-app -n myapp -c 827e3ef
+  gitopsctl --api-url http://127.0.0.1:9090 approve-app -n myapp -c 827e3ef`,
+	Args: cobra.NoArgs,
+	RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
+		msg, err := postAccepted(
+			fmt.Sprintf("/api/v1/applications/%s/approve", url.PathEscape(approveAppName)),
+			map[string]string{"commitHash": approveCommitHash},
+		)
+		if err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		emitCommandEvent(events.TypeAppSyncRequested, map[string]any{
+			"app":     approveAppName,
+			"commit":  approveCommitHash,
+			"api_url": apiBaseURL,
+		})
+		fmt.Println(msg)
+		return nil
+	},
+}
+
+func init() {
+	approveAppCmd.Flags().StringVarP(&approveAppName, "name", "n", "", "Application name (required)")
+	approveAppCmd.Flags().StringVarP(&approveCommitHash, "commit", "c", "", "Commit hash to approve (required)")
+	_ = approveAppCmd.MarkFlagRequired("name")
+	_ = approveAppCmd.MarkFlagRequired("commit")
+	rootCmd.AddCommand(approveAppCmd)
+}

+package cmd
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
+)
+
+func executeCommand(root *cobra.Command, args ...string) (output string, err error) {
+	buf := new(bytes.Buffer)
+	root.SetOut(buf)
+	root.SetErr(buf)
+	root.SetArgs(args)
+
+	err = root.Execute()
+	return buf.String(), err
+}
+
+func TestRootCommand(t *testing.T) {
+	root := RootCmd()
+	output, err := executeCommand(root, "--help")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Errorf("Unexpected error: %v", err)
+	}
+	if output == "" {
+		t.Error("Expected help output, got empty string")
+	}
+}
+
+func TestListAppsCommand(t *testing.T) {
+	root := RootCmd()
+	_, err := executeCommand(root, "list-apps")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Errorf("Unexpected error: %v", err)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestListClustersCommand(t *testing.T) {
+	root := RootCmd()
+	_, err := executeCommand(root, "list-clusters")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Errorf("Unexpected error: %v", err)

+func TestAppStatusCommand(t *testing.T) {

+}

+package cmd
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"encoding/json"
+	"fmt"
+	"io"
+	"net/http"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+)
+
+func postAccepted(path string, payload any) (string, error) {
+	return postExpecting(path, payload, http.StatusAccepted)
+}
+
+func postExpecting(path string, payload any, wantStatus int) (string, error) {
+	var body io.Reader
+	if payload != nil {
+		data, err := json.Marshal(payload)
+		if err != nil {
+			return "", err
+		}
+		body = bytes.NewReader(data)
+	}
+
+	req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, strings.TrimRight(apiBaseURL, "/")+path, body)
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+	if apiToken != "" {
+		req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+apiToken)
+	}
+	if payload != nil {
+		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
+	}
+
+	client := &http.Client{Timeout: 30 * time.Second}
+	resp, err := client.Do(req)
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("request failed: %w", err)
+	}
+	defer func() { _ = resp.Body.Close() }()
+
+	respBody, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
+	text := strings.TrimSpace(string(respBody))
+	if resp.StatusCode != wantStatus {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("unexpected status %s: %s", resp.Status, text)
+	}
+	return text, nil
+}

+package cmd
+
+import (
+	"io"
+	"net/http"
+	"net/http/httptest"
+	"testing"
+)
+
+func TestPostAccepted_SendsBearerTokenWhenConfigured(t *testing.T) {
+	origURL, origToken := apiBaseURL, apiToken
+	t.Cleanup(func() { apiBaseURL, apiToken = origURL, origToken })
+
+	var got string
+	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+		got = r.Header.Get("Authorization")
+		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusAccepted)
+	}))
+	defer srv.Close()
+	apiBaseURL = srv.URL
+
+	apiToken = ""
+	if _, err := postAccepted("/x", nil); err != nil || got != "" {
+		t.Fatalf("expected no auth header, got %q (%v)", got, err)
+	}
+	apiToken = "secret"
+	if _, err := postAccepted("/x", nil); err != nil || got != "Bearer secret" {
+		t.Fatalf("expected bearer header, got %q (%v)", got, err)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestPostAccepted(t *testing.T) {
+	tests := []struct {
+		name        string
+		status      int
+		payload     any
+		wantBody    string
+		wantContent string
+		wantErr     bool
+	}{
+		{name: "accepted without payload", status: http.StatusAccepted, wantBody: "ok"},
+		{name: "accepted with json payload", status: http.StatusAccepted, payload: map[string]string{"k": "v"}, wantBody: `{"k":"v"}`, wantContent: "application/json"},
+		{name: "non-accepted status is an error", status: http.StatusNotFound, wantErr: true},
+		{name: "unmarshalable payload", status: http.StatusAccepted, payload: make(chan int), wantErr: true},
+	}
+
+	orig := apiBaseURL
+	t.Cleanup(func() { apiBaseURL = orig })
+
+	for _, tc := range tests {
+		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			var gotBody, gotContent, gotMethod, gotPath string
+			srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+				b, _ := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
+				gotBody, gotContent, gotMethod, gotPath = string(b), r.Header.Get("Content-Type"), r.Method, r.URL.Path
+				w.WriteHeader(tc.status)
+				_, _ = w.Write([]byte("ok\n"))
+			}))
+			defer srv.Close()
+			apiBaseURL = srv.URL + "/"
+
+			out, err := postAccepted("/x/y", tc.payload)
+			if tc.wantErr {
+				if err == nil {
+					t.Fatalf("expected error, got output %q", out)
+				}
+				return
+			}
+			if err != nil {
+				t.Fatalf("unexpected error: %v", err)
+			}
+			if out != "ok" || gotMethod != http.MethodPost || gotPath != "/x/y" {
+				t.Fatalf("out=%q method=%s path=%s", out, gotMethod, gotPath)
+			}
+			if tc.payload != nil && (gotBody != tc.wantBody || gotContent != tc.wantContent) {
+				t.Fatalf("body=%q content-type=%q", gotBody, gotContent)
+			}
+			if tc.payload == nil && (gotBody != "" || gotContent != "") {
+				t.Fatalf("expected empty body/content-type, got %q %q", gotBody, gotContent)
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}

+package cmd
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"fmt"
+	"net/http"
+	"net/url"
+
+	apiapp "aeswibon.com/github/gitopsctl/internal/api/app"
+	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
+)
+
+var diffAppName string
+
+var planSymbols = map[string]string{
+	"create":    "+",
+	"update":    "~",
+	"prune":     "-",
+	"unchanged": "=",
+}
+
+var diffAppCmd = &cobra.Command{
+	Use:     "diff-app",
+	GroupID: "appGroup",
+	Short:   "Show what a sync would change for an application, without applying (via controller API)",
+	Long: `Asks a running gitopsctl controller to render the application's manifests from Git and compare them
+with the live cluster. Nothing is applied. Resources removed from Git are listed as prune candidates
+only when the application was registered with --prune.`,
+	Example: `
+  gitopsctl diff-app -n myapp
+  gitopsctl --api-url http://127.0.0.1:9090 --api-token "$TOKEN" diff-app -n myapp`,
+	Args: cobra.NoArgs,
+	RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
+		body, err := postExpecting(fmt.Sprintf("/api/v1/applications/%s/plan", url.PathEscape(diffAppName)), nil, http.StatusOK)
+		if err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		var plan apiapp.PlanResponse
+		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(body), &plan); err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("invalid plan response: %w", err)
+		}
+		printPlan(plan)
+		return nil
+	},
+}
+
+func printPlan(plan apiapp.PlanResponse) {
+	fmt.Printf("Plan for %s at %s\n", plan.App, plan.Commit)
+	counts := map[string]int{}
+	for _, item := range plan.Items {
+		counts[item.Action]++
+		fmt.Printf("  %s %-9s %s %s/%s\n", planSymbols[item.Action], item.Action, item.Kind, item.Namespace, item.Name)
+	}
+	fmt.Printf("%d to create, %d to update, %d to prune, %d unchanged\n",
+		counts["create"], counts["update"], counts["prune"], counts["unchanged"])
+}
+
+func init() {
+	diffAppCmd.Flags().StringVarP(&diffAppName, "name", "n", "", "Application name (required)")
+	_ = diffAppCmd.MarkFlagRequired("name")
+	rootCmd.AddCommand(diffAppCmd)
+}

+func captureStdout(t *testing.T, fn func()) string {
+	t.Helper()
+	orig := os.Stdout
+	r, w, err := os.Pipe()
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	os.Stdout = w
+	defer func() { os.Stdout = orig }()
+	fn()
+	_ = w.Close()

+	return string(out)

+package cmd
+
+import (
+	"context"
+
+	"aeswibon.com/github/gitopsctl/internal/events"
+	"go.uber.org/zap"
+)
+
+func commandEmitter() events.Emitter {
+	var sinks []events.Sink
+	if eventsFile != "" {
+		fs, err := events.NewFileSink(eventsFile)
+		if err != nil {
+			if logger != nil {
+				logger.Warn("failed to initialize events file sink", zap.Error(err))
+			}
+			return events.Noop{}
+		}
+		sinks = append(sinks, fs)
+	}
+	if eventsWebhookURL != "" {
+		sinks = append(sinks, events.NewWebhookSinkWithOptions(eventsWebhookURL, eventsWebhookBearer, events.WebhookOptions{
+			Timeout:       eventsWebhookTimeout,
+			Retries:       eventsWebhookRetry,
+			RetryBackoff:  eventsWebhookBackoff,
+			SigningSecret: eventsWebhookSecret,
+		}))
+	}
+	if len(sinks) == 0 {
+		return events.Noop{}
+	}
+	return events.NewBus(logger, "gitopsctl-cli", sinks...)
+}
+
+func emitCommandEvent(typ events.Type, data map[string]any) {
+	commandEmitter().Emit(context.Background(), typ, data)
+}

+package cmd
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"sort"
+	"strings"
+
+	"aeswibon.com/github/gitopsctl/internal/core/app"
+	"aeswibon.com/github/gitopsctl/internal/utils"
+	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
+	"go.uber.org/zap"
+)
+
+var listAppOpts utils.ListOptions
+
+var listAppCmd = &cobra.Command{
+	Use:     "list-apps",
+	GroupID: "appGroup",
+	Short:   "List all registered GitOps applications",
+	Long: `Displays information about all registered GitOps applications registered with gitopsctl.
+
+This command shows application names, repository URLs, branches, paths, clusters, and sync intervals.
+You can filter, sort, and format the output according to your needs.`,
+	Example: `
+  # List all registered applications in table format
+  gitopsctl list-apps
+
+  # List only active applications
+  gitopsctl list-apps --status active
+
+  # List applications sorted by name
+  gitopsctl list-apps --sort-by name
+
+  # Show detailed information for each application
+  gitopsctl list-apps --details
+
+  # Output as JSON for automation
+  gitopsctl list-apps --output json
+
+  # Compact view without headers
+  gitopsctl list-apps --no-header
+	`,
+	RunE: runListAppsCommand,
+}
+
+func runListAppsCommand(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
+	return utils.RunListCommand(
+		logger,
+		listAppOpts,
+		loadAppsForList,
+		filterAppsForList,
+		sortAppsForList,
+		handleEmptyAppsForList,
+	)
+}
+
+// loadAppsForList loads applications and converts them to cliutils.Renderable.
+func loadAppsForList() ([]utils.Renderable, error) {
+	apps, err := app.LoadApplications(app.DefaultAppConfigFile)
+	if err != nil {
+		logger.Error("Failed to load applications", zap.Error(err))
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to load applications: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	if len(apps.List()) == 0 {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("no applications registered")
+	}
+
+	logger.Info("Loaded applications successfully", zap.Int("count", len(apps.List())))
+	renderableApps := make([]utils.Renderable, len(apps.List()))
+	for i, a := range apps.List() {
+		renderableApps[i] = a
+	}
+	return renderableApps, nil
+}
+
+// filterAppsForList filters a slice of Renderable (app.Application) by status.
+func filterAppsForList(items []utils.Renderable, statusFilter string) []utils.Renderable {
+	if statusFilter == "" || strings.ToLower(statusFilter) == "all" {
+		return items
+	}
+
+	var filtered []utils.Renderable
+	targetStatus := strings.ToLower(statusFilter)
+
+	for _, item := range items {
+		if appItem, ok := item.(*app.Application); ok {
+			if strings.ToLower(appItem.Status) == targetStatus {
+				filtered = append(filtered, appItem)
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	return filtered
+}
+
+// sortAppsForList sorts a slice of Renderable (app.Application) by a given field.
+func sortAppsForList(items []utils.Renderable, sortField string) {
+	sort.Slice(items, func(i, j int) bool {
+		appI := items[i].(*app.Application)
+		appJ := items[j].(*app.Application)
+
+		switch strings.ToLower(sortField) {
+		case "status":
+			if appI.Status == appJ.Status {
+				return appI.Name < appJ.Name
+			}
+			return appI.Status < appJ.Status
+		case "branch":
+			if appI.Branch == appJ.Branch {
+				return appI.Name < appJ.Name
+			}
+			return appI.Branch < appJ.Branch
+		default: // Default to name
+			return appI.Name < appJ.Name
+		}
+	})
+}
+
+// handleEmptyAppsForList displays a message if no applications are found.
+func handleEmptyAppsForList(statusFilter string) error {
+	if statusFilter == "" || strings.ToLower(statusFilter) == "all" {
+		fmt.Println("📋 No apps registered yet")
+		fmt.Println("\n💡 Get started:")
+		fmt.Println("   gitopsctl register-apps --help")
+		fmt.Println("   gitopsctl register-cluster -n mycluster -k ~/.kube/config")
+		fmt.Println("   gitopsctl register-apps -n myapp -c mycluster -r <repo-url> -p <path>")
+	} else {
+		fmt.Printf("📋 No apps found with status '%s'\n", statusFilter)
+		fmt.Println("\n💡 Try:")
+		fmt.Println("   gitopsctl list-apps --status all")
+		fmt.Println("   gitopsctl list-apps")
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+func init() {
+	rootCmd.AddCommand(listAppCmd)
+	utils.AddListFlags(listAppCmd, &listAppOpts, "name")
+	_ = listAppCmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc("sort-by", func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
+		return []string{"name", "status", "branch"}, cobra.ShellCompDirectiveDefault
+	})
+}

+	}
+	if err := handleEmptyAppsForList("pending"); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("handleEmptyAppsForList(filtered) error = %v", err)

+}
+
+func TestFilterAppsForList(t *testing.T) {
+	items := []utils.Renderable{
+		&app.Application{Name: "a", Status: "active"},

+

+func TestSortAppsForList(t *testing.T) {
